title: Redwood Signal: Instrumented Cost & Quality Advisor — Product Overview and Rollout Playbook
author: Ayesha Patel
content:
Overview:

Redwood Signal is an opinionated product layer that correlates per-route telemetry (latency, token mix, cache hit rates, model variant performance) with consumption economics and quality impact. The goal is to give product and platform engineers concrete, actionable recommendations to reduce unit cost while preserving user-facing quality. Redwood Signal is intended to operate alongside Redwood Optimize: Optimize provides bulk simulation and suggestions; Signal provides live, instrumented recommendations and automated guardrails tied to observed behavior.

Goals:
- Surface the highest-impact opportunities to reduce per-token cost without regressing quality (target: >=15% unit cost reduction for 60% of participating tenants in first 90 days).
- Provide deterministic rollback and safety controls (canary percentage, quality canaries, auto-fallback).
- Integrate into the Console and API for one-click adoption of recommended packaging/quantization/batching profiles.
- Offer a beta pricing advisor for enterprise customers to evaluate trade-offs with shadow mode before committing to Dedicated/Private changes.

Primary user personas:
- ML Engineers: want to preserve model fidelity while reducing GPU spend.
- Platform/Product engineers: want cost forecasts tied to SLOs and consumption tiers.
- Customer Success / Solutions: want playbooks for negotiation and migration guidance.

Scope (MVP):
- Ingest per-route telemetry from Console and tracing (latency distribution, tokens per request, model variant used, cache hit rate).
- Run lightweight offline simulations for batching, quantization, and fallback variants to estimate cost/latency/quality deltas.
- Present ranked recommendations in Console with confidence bands and an impact estimate (tokens saved, $/month).
- Provide an API endpoint for programmatic retrieval of recommendations and a one-click apply flow for non-breaking changes (e.g., batching policy adjustments).

Non-goals (MVP):
- Not a replacement for full Redwood Optimize eval pipelines (heavy offline evals, human-in-the-loop quality judgments).
- Not performing model retraining or synthetic data generation.

Requirements (high level, MVP):
1) Data and telemetry:
   - Ingest: per-request metadata (route id, model id, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms_p50/p95/p99, failure_flag, cache_hit boolean) at 1-min rollup.
   - Retention for recommendations: 90 days of high-resolution, 1 year of aggregated monthly buckets.

2) SLOs and thresholds for advisor recommendations:
   - Quality safety: regressions must be detectable via route-level eval set or user-defined golden prompts; auto-apply only if projected quality delta <= 0.5% end-to-end metric degradation unless explicitly accepted.
   - Latency SLO preservation: projected p95 must remain within customer-configured delta (default +20%).

3) API contract:
   - GET /v1/signal/recommendations?route_id=<id>&window=7d => returns ranked recommendation list (type, estimated_savings, confidence).
   - POST /v1/signal/apply => idempotent apply for allowed recommendations.

4) Security & governance:
   - RBAC: only owners and roles with 'advisor_apply' may execute one-click applies.
   - Audit logging for any automated changes with clear revert identifiers.

Design summary:
- Data pipeline: streaming traces -> enrichment service (resolves model variant metadata, customer config) -> feature store (per-route aggregates) -> recommendation engine.
- Recommendation engine: ensemble of three strategies: rules-based (safe conservative changes), simulation-based (batch/quantization simulation using historical token/latency distributions), and policy-driven ML ranker (learns impact from past applied recommendations).
- Safety layer: each candidate recommendation passes through an evaluation policy that checks: quality thresholds, dependency matrix (model compatibilities), and capacity constraints (if change increases resource demand).

Operational SLOs and telemetry (for platform):
- Recommendation generation latency: <= 5 min for 24h window scans (background jobs).
- API request latency: 99th < 300ms for GET recommendations.
- False-positive rate (post-apply rollback rate) goal: < 5% within first 30 days.
- Monitoring: coverage for inference-telemetry ingestion success, enrich service lag, simulation job failures, and apply/revert audit trails.

Roadmap & milestones (quarterly):
Q3 2026 (Beta internal):
- Instrumentation hooks in Console, implement basic rules-based advisor, expose GET recommendations, launch internal beta with 10 customers.
Q4 2026 (External beta):
- Simulation engine for batching and 8-bit quantization suggestions, add POST apply with canary flow, start closed external beta with select enterprise accounts.
Q1 2027 (GA):
- Integrations with Dedicated/Private apply flows, cost-first packaging suggestions, add per-tenant safety profiles and reporting templates.
Q2 2027+:
- ML ranker improvements and feedback loop (learn from applied recommendation outcomes), marketplace add-on packaging, predictive forecasting for seasonal workloads.

Pricing & packaging approach:
- Beta period: no additional charge (encouraged to provide feedback).
- GA pricing model: two optional add-ons: Advisor Insights (read-only recommendations, billed per-route per-month) and Advisor Automation (apply capabilities, billed per-successful-apply + delta-savings share opt-in).
- For enterprise Dedicated/Private customers: optional professional services for migration and safety-proofing (fixed-fee + success bonus).
- Pricing examples (illustrative):
   - Small tenant (10 active routes): Advisor Insights $200/month; Automation opt-in $0 + 10% of first-month realized savings (if > $1,000).
   - Large enterprise (500 routes): tiered discounts and SLA options; custom contract negotiation recommended.

Rollout playbook (one-line, then steps):
- Goal: enable safe adoption with measurable rollback capability and metrics to evaluate success.

Steps:
1) Onboard telemetry: ensure route-level tracing is turned on for the target tenant. Verify ingestion (ingest_success = true for last 72h).
2) Baseline snapshot: capture a 14-day baseline for tokens, latency, and gold prompts evaluation.
3) Shadow recommendations: run recommendations in shadow (no apply) for 7 days, collect simulated outcomes.
4) Stakeholder review: present top 5 recommendations, expected savings, and quality confidence to tenant engineering/CS.
5) Canary apply: apply to 1% traffic for 24–72h with automatic rollback on quality/latency breach.
6) Ramp & monitor: if no regression, ramp to 10% -> 50% -> 100% with incremental checks.
7) Postmortem and learning: log outcomes totraining dataset to improve ML ranker.

Quick API example (GET recommendation snippet):
curl -X GET "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/signal/recommendations?route_id=orders-v2&window=14d" \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>'

Sample response (truncated, illustrative):
{
  "recommendations": [
    {
      "id": "rec-20261004-1",
      "type": "batching_tweak",
      "description": "Increase max_batch_wait_ms from 5 -> 12 for route orders-v2",
      "estimated_monthly_savings": "$1,830",
      "confidence": "0.78"
    }
  ]
}

Release notes (v0.1-beta, 2026-11-02):
- Initial internal beta release.
- Console panel for Signal with top-10 ranked recommendations and simulation delta charts.
- Read-only API endpoints for recommendations.
- Rules engine providing safe batching and caching policy suggestions.
- Known issues: simulation underestimates tail-latency impact on bursty routes; working on integrated p99-aware simulation in Q4 2026.

Appendix — Data model excerpts and constraints:
- Route record schema (rollup 1m): route_id, tenant_id, timestamp_min, tokens_in_sum, tokens_out_sum, requests_count, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, cache_hits, model_variant_counts.
- Recommendation record (immutable): rec_id, route_id, created_at, strategy, estimated_savings_usd, estimated_quality_delta_pct, state (shadow|proposed|applied|reverted).

Open questions & risks:
- How to attribute savings in multi-tenant shared Dedicated pools when changes alter cross-tenant batching? (short-term: per-route attribution with caveats; long-term: shared pool attribution model).
- Customer appetite for savings-share pricing (needs legal/finance guidance).
- Accuracy of simulation when tenant traffic is highly spiky — mitigations: conservative defaults and forced longer shadow periods.
